item.title: U.S.-Iran tensions intensify amid regional calls for restraint
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
TEHRAN/WASHINGTON, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- Tensions between Iran and the United States have escalated in recent days amid military clashes and maritime incidents near the Strait of Hormuz, while regional countries stepped up diplomatic efforts to ease the situation. Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) said Saturday its aerospace division has established underground missile and drone production facilities and is continuously increasing the range of its missiles. "We will not stop in this regard," IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told a press conference, adding that the corps is prepared to defend the country "without any geographical limitation" if the enemy renews strikes. His remarks come amid heightened U.S. threats of military action against Iran, and as the U.S. Army reportedly carried out "minor" attacks targeting Iran's southern Qeshm Island. Earlier on Saturday, local media reported that two missiles hit Qeshm Island, while Iran's air defence force shot down two U.S. MQ-9 drones. U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that U.S. forces launched new strikes targeting Iran's air defense systems, describing the military action as "minor." This was the second strike reportedly carried out by the United States against the Iranian island this week. The Wall Street Journal, citing U.S. officials, reported Tuesday that the United States attacked the island on Monday. Meanwhile, the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said late Friday that the United States is offering a reward of up to 20 million U.S. dollars and "possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program. Iran has said that uranium enrichment is an "inseparable" part of the country's nuclear industry, and that Iran's nuclear program is in compliance with its safeguards agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency and the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons. Tensions at sea also escalated around the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said on Friday morning that two "violating" oil tankers seeking to transit the strait through an "unauthorized" route caught fire after hitting naval mines. Its navy warned that bids by CENTCOM forces to compel oil tankers to cross the waterway through the mined route will lead to nothing but "consecutive and abject" defeats. As hostilities intensified, regional countries stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert a wider conflict, while Tehran engaged in active outreach to secure strategic support and coordinate de-escalation steps. Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Mohsen Rezaei met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, delivering a message from Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Rezaei said Putin strongly condemned the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran and expressed his country's readiness to provide any assistance necessary to help bring the war to an end. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Thursday held several phone calls with his counterparts from Oman, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Kuwait to discuss ongoing diplomatic processes. During a phone conversation, Araghchi and Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi stressed the importance of consolidating sustainable understandings to ensure maritime security, end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region. In Doha, Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani spoke by phone with Trump on Friday to discuss ongoing diplomatic efforts to ease regional tensions and reach a comprehensive agreement to end the crisis. To facilitate direct engagement, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein proposed on Friday the establishment of a regional foreign ministers' committee to visit Tehran and Washington to help de-escalate regional tensions and resolve existing differences. Meanwhile, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, held phone calls on Thursday and Friday to review joint efforts to defuse tensions, calling for restraint and dialogue to avoid further escalation. Despite the diplomatic flurry, Iranian officials maintained that progress depends on concrete U.S. actions. SNSC Deputy Secretary Ali Bagheri Kani said Friday that Iran needs to see practical measures by the United States rather than mere "paper commitments," stressing that efforts must be made to make the United States implement Iran's proposed plan for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.■

item.title: 7th World Media Summit opens in Beijing, highlighting media transformation in AI age
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
* The 7th World Media Summit held its opening ceremony in Beijing on Saturday under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." * At the summit, delegates discussed the role of the media in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) and how the industry should respond to the challenges it poses. * The 7th World Media Summit Beijing Consensus was adopted at the ceremony, calling for joint efforts to advance the transformation and development of the global media industry in the AI era. BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- The 7th World Media Summit held its opening ceremony in Beijing on Saturday under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." Xinhua News Agency and the Beijing municipal government jointly organized this year's summit, which runs from Thursday to Monday. It drew nearly 500 representatives from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks and government bodies from 112 countries and regions, as well as the United Nations and other international organizations. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, also addressed the ceremony. At the summit, delegates discussed the role of the media in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) and how the industry should respond to the challenges it poses. They called for closer cooperation to broaden access to advanced technologies and help media organizations worldwide develop together, while urging concrete steps to uphold journalistic ethics and safeguard the authenticity of news content as AI use expands. INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT Addressing the opening ceremony, Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, called on media professionals to share new technologies and applications, exchange experience in using them, and close gaps in AI research, development and understanding. "We should lead the way in ensuring that all media professionals have a fair chance to benefit from AI," he said. The 7th World Media Summit Beijing Consensus was adopted at the ceremony. It calls for joint efforts to advance the transformation and development of the global media industry in the AI era. Recognizing AI's growing role in media development, the consensus commits to advancing the inclusive and responsible application of AI in the media sector so that advances in AI benefit media organizations at all stages of development and in every country. AFP Chairman Fabrice Fries also stressed the need for inclusive AI development at the summit. "The benefits of this technological revolution should extend far beyond a small number of companies or countries," he said. Fries called on media organizations, governments, businesses and universities to work together to ensure that AI helps build a healthier, more diverse global information ecosystem. In particular, AI models must be trained on datasets that reflect the diversity of human societies and perspectives, he said. The World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is now a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The previous summit was held in 2024 in Urumqi, the capital city of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. For participants from Global South countries, the summit is particularly important in helping their media organizations adapt to the digital era and narrow development gaps. Abdishakur Ali Ahmed, director of communication strategy at the Somalian Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism, said the summit provides a platform for discussion about navigating digital transformation, which is central to Africa's development. "The summit also offered us a chance to see China's digital transformation firsthand," he said, expressing hope that Somalia and other African countries would deepen cooperation with China to respond to shared challenges. Luis Alves do Rosario Canhemba, senior director of the Information Office of Mozambique, said stronger international cooperation was essential for the country to facilitate its ongoing digital transformation. He called for more exchanges on technology and joint efforts to address AI-related risks in the media industry, and expected expanded mutually beneficial cooperation between Mozambique and China as well as other Global South countries. JOINTLY ADDRESSING RISKS As AI is reshaping the entire chain of news production at an unprecedented speed, it has brought opportunities but also risks and challenges to the media industry, such as ethical lapses in the use of technology and the proliferation of false information, Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua, said at the Summit on Saturday. "We should take the initiative to share technological expertise, open-source models and training resources, and work together to strengthen our capacity to address risks arising from AI," he said. On Saturday, the summit also released the Global Media Initiative for the Joint Development of AI Application Standards. Launched by Xinhua, the initiative brings together major media outlets and other professional organizations to safeguard the authenticity of information, protect data security, and uphold media ethics, thereby maintaining public trust in the media. The first 22 participants also include Russia's TASS News Agency, the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), South Africa's Independent Media, and China's People's Daily and China Media Group. Under the initiative, participants plan to work together for about two years to develop a set of standards that address different media uses of AI and are validated by media outlets. The initiative also calls for a global database of AI applications. Dejan Jazvic, editor-in-chief of the Federal News Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, welcomed the summit's efforts to address AI-related challenges. "The standardization of AI applications must be established as soon as possible," he said. "It is of crucial importance that we harness AI to improve and develop the media, rather than allowing it to serve as a replacement for media or as a tool for manipulating and deceiving the public," he said. Mohammed Alyami, director general of the Union of News Agencies of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, said the theme of this year's summit, "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action," called on media organizations to build on shared commitments by proposing practical initiatives and forging partnerships. He proposed an international framework for responsible journalism in the AI era, grounded in transparency, reliability and information verification. Media organizations should ensure that technological change serves people and that the media always play a role as a bridge for mutual understanding and a platform for sharing the truth, he said. ■

item.title: Media executive calls for greater cooperation, human oversight in AI-driven journalism
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
ISTANBUL, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- Artificial intelligence (AI) is opening up new possibilities for journalism, but media organizations must strengthen cooperation to ensure technological advances go hand in hand with reliable reporting, said Sumeyra Teymur, CEO of Turkish news platform Haberler.com. In an interview ahead of the 7th World Media Summit, Teymur praised China's innovative use of AI in journalism, saying she was impressed by the country's efforts to integrate advanced technologies into the media industry. "I heard about and saw AI anchors presenting news during my previous visit, which really impressed me," she said. "I have always loved technology, and these developments make me excited. I am always thinking about what is coming next." She also expressed interest in the potential use of humanoid robots to cover dangerous situations, such as earthquakes and conflicts, where deploying human reporters could pose risks. Haberler.com has also integrated AI into its daily operations. Receiving more than 2,000 news articles from various sources every day, the platform uses AI to organize content, generate headlines and supplement articles with relevant photos and videos, enabling its editorial team to handle a larger volume of news. However, Teymur stressed that human oversight remains essential, warning that AI can make mistakes and facilitate the creation of fabricated news, images and videos, as well as the manipulation of voices and identities. "Whenever we use AI, we always have a human checking the content," she said, emphasizing the responsibility of media organizations to verify information before publication. She called for stronger international media cooperation in sharing information, technological expertise and cultural stories, noting that no single organization can tackle the rapid spread of misinformation across borders alone. The 7th World Media Summit, hosted by Xinhua News Agency and the Beijing Municipal People's Government under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action," is being held in Beijing from Nov. 5 to 9. Teymur said she looked forward to exchanging experience with Chinese journalists and strengthening ties with Chinese media organizations. ■

item.title: China Focus: From products to partnerships, CIIE sets stage for global debuts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
People walk past an billboard themed on the ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 5, 2026. The expo, the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, opened here on Thursday. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. Total exhibition area exceeds 440,000 square meters this year. (Xinhua/Xing Guangli) SHANGHAI, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- For many global businesses, unveiling a new product or technology is more than showcasing innovation. It is also about reaching the right market. Austrian machine tool maker WFL Millturn Technologies knows this well. To make its Asian debut, the company's massive new machining center crossed continents and oceans, traveling for more than two months before arriving in Shanghai for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE). "This visit to the CIIE will allow us to gain a close-up understanding of the development opportunities brought by the upgrading of China's high-end manufacturing industry," said Mayr Günther Franz Josef, WFL's general manager. A first-time participant at the expo, the company also hopes to deepen cooperation and strengthen ties with industrial partners across the Asia-Pacific region. WFL's journey speaks to the CIIE's appeal as a proven platform for global businesses to launch debuts and connect markets, innovation and industries. Now in its ninth edition, this year's CIIE is seeing more than 480 exhibits making their global, Asian or China debuts. The number sets a new record for the event, which has seen over 3,400 new products, technologies and services debut in the past eight editions. Many of them moved from the expo floor to store shelves and became bestsellers in the Chinese market. For French cosmetics giant L'Oréal, the CIIE is an ideal launchpad for new brands, new products, new innovations, and new partnerships. "Nearly half of our brands made their debut in the Chinese market through the CIIE," said Lan Zhenzhen, chief corporate affairs and engagement officer, L'Oréal North Asia & China. She added that these brands have since performed well in China. In China's five-year development blueprint for 2026-2030, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, as well as actively promoting the "debut economy." "The Chinese market is a barometer for global product trends and innovation," said Xia Xianlin, account director at Joy Wing Mau Chile Spa. Introducing a new coconut product at the expo, the company hopes to leverage the CIIE's spillover effect to help more fruit products enter the Chinese market. At the CIIE, debuts do more than introduce new products. They spark further innovation as technologies and ideas from around the world meet local needs and partners. Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk, which has participated in all the previous eight editions of the expo, is showcasing new medicines at this year's event, including Kyinsu, a once-weekly injection for type 2 diabetes. "The CIIE has become an important part of our work in China," said Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo Nordisk. This is the company's ninth consecutive year at the CIIE, and many medicines first showcased at the expo have since reached the Chinese market. According to Novo Nordisk, Chinese experts have helped develop Kyinsu, serving as lead investigators in its global Phase III clinical trial and helping shape the global research. In telecommunications, U.S. tech company Qualcomm debuted the world's first 6G terminal prototype outside the laboratory. According to the company, the device has been used in 6G technology tests and validation conducted with its Chinese partners, including China Mobile and ZTE. "Qualcomm's participation in the CIIE is more than a number of visits. It reflects our journey of innovating and growing together with our Chinese partners," said Frank Meng, chairman of Qualcomm China. Unveiling a tire made with 75 percent renewable and recycled materials at the CIIE, French tire manufacturer Michelin has described its evolving approach to China as a shift from "In China, for China" to "With China, for the World." New trends and technologies in sectors ranging from electric vehicles to autonomous driving often emerge in China ahead of other markets, according to Jay Wu, Michelin China vice president, director of government relations and strategy. "China is both a test ground and a gym, a place where we test new ideas, challenge ourselves and continuously strengthen our innovation capabilities," Wu told Xinhua. ■

item.title: Xiplomacy: Xi's reply inspires Australian students to carry forward friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
ADELAIDE, Australia, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- As spring unfolds in the Southern Hemisphere, a message of friendship has crossed the ocean. Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship. In his letter dated Oct. 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students recently visited China to take part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, engaged in in-depth exchanges, forged friendships that transcended borders, and created wonderful memories together. For many of the young Australians, the visit was more than a sporting and cultural exchange. It offered an opportunity to see China firsthand, connect with their Chinese peers and gain a deeper appreciation of the country. Xi's reply has given their experience added significance, resonating with both the students and education professionals who helped make the exchange possible. In July 2025, Xi met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Stressing the importance of cultivating people-to-people ties, Xi said Australians from all walks of life are welcome to visit the country and China stands ready to invite more Australian youth for exchange programs. The invitation was taken up in September, when more than 100 students and staff members from six leading Australian universities, including the University of Sydney, Adelaide University and the University of New South Wales, visited China. In China's eastern city of Nanjing, the young Australians joined students from Chinese universities, including Nanjing University and Tongji University, for the rowing and dragon boat event. Beyond the competition, the event also offered participants a chance to appreciate China's traditional dragon boat culture. The connections made during the trip did not end when the students returned home. After their trip to China, the students jointly wrote a letter to Xi and Albanese, sharing their experiences during their visit, expressing admiration for China's long-lasting history and rich culture, as well as its scientific and technological innovation capabilities. They also voiced their eagerness to help carry forward the bilateral friendship and foster greater mutual understanding. On Friday, Xi's reply was presented to representatives of the young Australians in Adelaide, South Australia's capital. For Daniel Wiersema, a student representative from Adelaide University, receiving the letter was a particularly moving moment. Recalling the visit to China, he expressed gratitude to Xi for the opportunity and the experience. "We want to thank him, and hope that our countries can become really, really good friends in the future," he said. Jason Slater, head of Sport Development at Adelaide University Sport and Fitness, said he had spoken with students from all the participating Australian universities and found that they indeed enjoyed the trip. The letter to the two leaders brought together the students' individual experiences and reflections, conveying personal stories and a strong sense of friendship, he said. Xi's reply was "very important encouragement," Slater said. Many participants now hoped to return to China for further studies and explore opportunities to build connections with the country in their future careers, he said. Elise Courtney, a student at the University of New South Wales, recalled her excitement at receiving Xi's reply. "We know how busy it must be for him to take the time to reply to us. It was really special," she said. She also showed Xinhua a team jersey she had swapped with a Chinese teammate, describing it as a treasured keepsake of the trip. In their letter, the students recalled seeing China's dynamic, modern cities while also experiencing its rich history and cultural heritage. The contrast and combination left a strong impression on them. Beyond the individual memories, the exchange also brought home a broader message about the role of young people in shaping bilateral relations. China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi noted in the letter, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation. He voiced hope that the Australian students can continue to actively contribute to the cause of friendship between the two countries, serve as torchbearers of the friendship and cooperation between the two countries, and carry forward this friendship from generation to generation. For Anja Felderhof, a student from Adelaide University, that message struck a particular chord. "That was my take-away sentence," she said. "All of my friends in Australia can say we're pretty excited to continue this friendship as well," she added. The importance of such exchanges extends beyond the students themselves, offering universities an opportunity to build lasting institutional links. Rongyu Li, deputy vice-chancellor and vice-president (global engagement) of the University of Queensland, told Xinhua that face-to-face exchanges among young people from the two countries can deepen mutual understanding and foster friendship. He said Xi's reply would encourage more Australian universities to actively participate in exchanges and further strengthen cooperation with China.■

item.title: CPC initiates election process for delegates to 21st national congress
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has released a circular for the election of delegates to the Party's 21st national congress, making comprehensive plans for related work. The Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee has made detailed arrangements for the election, according to an official statement released Saturday. The CPC will convene its 21st national congress in the second half of 2027 in Beijing, the 20th CPC Central Committee decided at its fifth plenary session in late October. The congress comes at a critical time when the CPC has been working to basically realize socialist modernization and heading toward the Second Centenary Goal. It will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country, the statement said. The election of the delegates will lay an important foundation for the success of this congress, it said. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, convened meetings of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee to study the matter in depth and set out overall requirements, objectives and tasks for carrying out the work, according to the statement. A total of 2,360 delegates to the congress will be elected by 38 electoral units across the country, the statement said. It urged putting political standards first, applying strict eligibility criteria, following rigorous electoral procedures, and strictly enforcing electoral discipline, to ensure that those elected are of high caliber, well-structured in composition, and broadly representative, with the support of Party members. The statement stressed the importance of examining candidates' political stance and awareness, as well as their capacity for political judgment, thinking and implementation. It also called for strict scrutiny of candidates' integrity and conduct. Front-line workers should account for an appropriate proportion of the delegates. Efforts must be made to recommend model workers, farmers and professionals as candidates in the election. Women Party members and Party members from ethnic minority groups should each make up a certain proportion of the delegates. The delegates should come from a wide range of fields, including the economy, science and technology, national defense, law enforcement and the justice system, education, public communication, culture, health, sports and social administration. The delegates should also include workers in new forms of employment, the statement said. The delegates will be elected through a process in which the number of candidates must exceed the number of seats by more than 15 percent. The statement stressed the need to ensure oversight throughout the electoral process and maintain zero tolerance for violations of rules, discipline and laws. Any violation should be resolutely investigated and dealt with, it added. It urged making the election a process of studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, particularly Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. The election will run from now until the end of June 2027. ■
